definition: DuckDB is an in-process analytical SQL database: run fast SQL over CSV, Parquet or DataFrames with no server.
details: Created by Mark Raasveldt and Hannes Mühleisen at CWI Amsterdam in 2019; stewarded by the DuckDB Foundation and DuckDB Labs.

explainer.lead: How to install DuckDB, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.createdBy: Created by Mark Raasveldt and Hannes Mühleisen at CWI; DuckDB Labs.

quickstart.python:
import duckdb

print(duckdb.sql("""
    SELECT label, count(*) AS n
    FROM 'train.parquet'
    GROUP BY label
""").df())

explainer.inAi: Inspect and slice evaluation logs or training data with SQL; the vss extension even adds vector similarity search.

tiers.eli5: It is a portable toolbox you open on your own desk to run big queries, instead of mailing the work to a warehouse.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for local analytics, data wrangling and embedded querying inside applications and notebooks. A pitfall is expecting it to serve as a multi-user transactional server database; it is designed for in-process analytical work.
tiers.paperLevel: DuckDB is an in-process analytical SQL database executing queries over files such as CSV and Parquet and over DataFrames. Limits: it is an analytical, embedded engine rather than a multi-user transactional server.

explainer.example: A notebook loads a directory of Parquet files and runs SQL aggregations directly on them in-process with no database server.
